issues.title: The shaping loop turns a business intent into a testable slice, its plan and its eval
issues.body:
Capability: the shaping loop (ADR 049) gets a business intent and turns it into three things, one play each: `/shape-slice` shapes a slice a person can test end to end; the plan play makes a plan that can be run and tracked; the eval play builds an eval that tests whether the business intent is met. The person approves once, at the end of the loop, before anything goes to the tracker.

## Results
1. An eval that tests whether the slice delivers its business intent, from the outside, on its surface. It tests what is known at that time (the UX design may not be known yet).
2. A plan that is ready to run and can be tracked: the epic and one story per feature, each carrying what an agent needs to build it.

## Not in this capability
- Design, build, test and validate of an epic. These moved to their own business intent (decided 2026-10-23).

## Links
- Serves: #788

Represents: sl-intent-to-design

## Feature-to-story map

- fn-795 → #795
- fn-818 → #818
- fn-798 → #798

issues.title: /shape-slice grills within the tier and assembles the slice that delivers the business intent
issues.body:
Feature: `/shape-slice` gets a business intent, grills the person within the grilling tier, and puts together the slice that delivers the intent. It writes the slice into the product model with its link to the intent.

## Done when
- It takes a business intent issue number as its entry point, finds that intent in the product model, and works from the model. If the model has no page for it, it writes the page from the issue. It does not need a slice that the seven lenses stamped "realized".
- It reads the product model and memory first, and asks only about the gaps — all at once, each question standing alone — within the tier's budget (#817). It records the answers in short-term memory.
- It picks the features that serve the intent, from any capability, and names the person who tests the slice and the one surface they test it on. A slice with no such surface is not written.
- It finds a slice that already serves the intent before it makes a new one.
- It fills the model as it goes: a domain, capability, feature or ICE the slice needs and the model lacks is added at the depth it knows, never skipped.
- It writes the slice (`features` in build order, `vertical`, `intents`) into the spine's `slices` list, with its record at `product-os/slices/<id>.yaml` (a slice links to capabilities, and through them to its domains; it has no domain home), and the grounding linter passes.
- Until #796, it shows the slice at a typed checkpoint (yes / change / stop) and commits only after yes.
- Built fresh with `/create-play` (the old play's job, cutting epics, is gone; decisions: `.garura/project/issues/795/context/decisions.md`).

## Not in this issue
- The eval (#798), the plan (#818), the pinned checkpoint (#796), the tier setting (#817).
- The design, build and test of the epic (the build-stage business intent).

## Links
- Serves: #788
- Part of: #794
- Needs: #816

## Scope of work

Goals:
- When the product owner runs /shape-slice on a business intent, the spine gets one slice that serves that intent, with its features in build order, its one surface and the persona who tests it.
- One person can test the slice end to end on that one surface.
- The same run puts the slice's hidden file in the plan's evals folder, with one entry for each feature of the slice and each entry closed by exactly one way back. This part is not built yet; decision 6 adds it.

Limits:
- Write only the slice, its link to the business intent it serves, its record, the model parts the slice lacks (each marked to be deepened) and the hidden file.
- Write no plan, epic, story or eval.
- Put the hidden file only in .garura/project/plans/<plan-id>/evals/<slug>/.
- The confirmation the product owner sees shows the slice only.
- Ask the product owner only what the product model and memory do not answer, and stay inside the question tier.

Expectations:
- The product owner runs /shape-slice 788 in Claude Code and finds one slice in the spine and the hidden file in plans/788/evals/<slug>/.
- No other new file appears outside the product model.
- Run on a real business intent, the play writes one slice and its hidden file, and no plan, epic, story or eval.

## Context guidance

- Read: the business intent's page, the spine, the Slice kind in the ontology, memory, and the play's own folder in core/components/plays/shape-slice/ (built in #795)
- Never read: the plan, its epics and stories, and the eval: they come after this play
- Persona: the product owner, who names the intent, answers the questions and approves in Claude Code; /shape-plan and /shape-eval read the slice after
- In and out: in: the intent page when the model has none, the questions, reuse of a slice that already serves, the missing model parts, the slice, its record and its hidden file, and the stop at a typed yes, change or stop; out: the plan, the epic, the stories and the eval

Represents: fn-795

issues.title: The plan play makes the plan file, the epic and one story per feature
issues.body:
Feature: the **plan play** is the second play of the shaping loop (ADR 049). It runs right after `/shape-slice`, with no stop between them. It makes the plan for the business intent: the plan file, one epic for the slice and one story for each feature. It writes nothing in the evals folder: /shape-slice writes the slice's hidden file (ontology v11, ADR 052). Each story carries what an agent needs to build it, and the plan can be tracked.

## Done when
- A new play (built with `/create-play`) takes the slice `/shape-slice` wrote and writes `.garura/project/plans/<business intent>.yaml` — the one plan for that intent; a second slice for the same intent joins the same plan (ontology Q30).
- It makes, in the tracker, one epic for the slice, and one story for each feature of the slice as a sub-issue of the epic.
- Each story holds the goal, the limits, the Context guidance and the expectations from its feature's ICE and its capability's ICE, and never a failure or recovery condition (ontology v11, ADR 049 §4, ADR 052).
- The epic keeps the feature-to-story map: an entry for each feature, with the story that delivers it. It agrees with the plan's Tree.
- It finds the epic and stories that exist before it makes new ones. A second run makes no duplicates.
- When a feature leaves the slice after its plan exists, its story moves out of the plan; the plan play does not delete it, and the story stays in the tracker. A feature that comes in gets one story (the product owner's answer Q-change-1, /shape-slice run #866).
- The epic is in the tracker only; the spine `epics` list and `epic.md` pages leave the product model.

## Not in this issue
- The eval (#798) and the one checkpoint for the loop (#796).
- Building the epic (the build-stage business intent).

## Links
- Serves: #788
- Part of: #794
- Needs: #795

## Scope of work

Goals:
- When the product owner runs /shape-plan on a business intent, the intent's one plan file (.garura/project/plans/<intent>.yaml) exists, with one epic for each slice that serves the intent and one story for each feature of that slice.
- The plan names every capability and feature it holds, each with its ICE.
- A second run finds the plan, the epics and the stories that exist, and makes no copies of them.

Limits:
- Write only the plan file, the epics and the stories.
- Each story holds the goals, the limits, the expectations and the Context guidance from its feature's ICE and that feature's capability's ICE, and nothing from the hidden file.
- The hidden file and all that it holds belong to /shape-slice (decision 6); the eval belongs to /shape-eval.
- Nothing goes to the tracker before the product owner types yes.
- Do not pick, rank or test slices; the product owner chose the slice at /shape-slice.
- Do not wait for a full product model; write a missing model page as a light page during the run.

Expectations:
- The product owner runs /shape-plan 788 in Claude Code after /shape-slice and finds the plan file, one epic, and one story for each feature of the slice.
- No story holds any line from the hidden file.
- Building the plans for #717 and its partner gives the same trees that were filed by hand on 2026-10-21.

## Context guidance

- Read: the slice in the spine, and the ICE of each feature and of its capability, once for each story
- Never read: the slice's hidden file and the evals folder
- Persona: the product owner, who runs and tracks the plan; the build play reads the stories after
- In and out: in: the plan file in .garura/project/plans/ and the tracker's epics and stories; out: picking the slice, the hidden file, the eval and the build (not built yet, #818)

Represents: fn-818

issues.title: The eval play writes the slice's eval: is the business intent met, tested on the slice's surface
issues.body:
Feature: the **eval play** is the third play of the shaping loop (ADR 049). It runs after the plan play and builds the slice's eval: does the slice deliver its business intent? The eval tests from the outside, on the slice's one surface, and no builder can read it.

## Done when
- A new play (built with `/create-play`) reads the epic, its stories and the slice's hidden failure-and-recovery file, and never the ICE directly (ontology v10, Q29). It never reads the usage guide or the code when it builds the eval.
- It writes the eval into `.garura/project/plans/<plan-id>/evals/<slug>/`, which no builder reads (CLAUDE.md).
- Each check is black-box: when the eval runs after the build, it reaches the slice only through its usage guide (`guides/<slug>.md`) and checks that every goal and expectation is met and no failure condition happens. It says what it cannot test yet.
- When a check fails, the eval writes a handoff plan that names the symptom, never the failure condition or the check.
- For Garura, the surface is often a play, so the eval runs the play on a test project (Griffin is the first candidate).

## Not in this issue
- Running the eval, and encrypting it (#828).
- The one checkpoint for the loop (#796).

## Links
- Serves: #788
- Part of: #794
- Needs: #818

## Scope of work

Goals:
- When the product owner runs /shape-eval on a business intent, the slice's evals folder holds one eval for that slice.
- The eval checks from the outside, on the slice's surface, each goal and expectation of the stories, and checks that nothing the hidden file warns about happens.
- The eval says if the business intent is met on the slice's surface.

Limits:
- Read only the epic, its stories and the slice's hidden file.
- Never read an ICE page, the usage guide or the code.
- Write the eval only in the plan's evals folder (.garura/project/plans/<plan-id>/evals/<slug>/), and nowhere else.

Expectations:
- The product owner runs /shape-eval 788 in Claude Code after /shape-plan and finds the eval in plans/788/evals/<slug>/.
- No build play's inputs name the evals folder.

## Context guidance

- Read: the epic and the stories that /shape-plan wrote, and the hidden file that /shape-slice wrote
- Never read: any ICE page, the usage guide (guides/<slug>.md) and the code
- Persona: the product owner, who wants proof that the intent is met; the running eval after the build uses what this play writes
- In and out: in: writing the eval, which for Garura often runs a play on a test project and reaches the slice only through its usage guide; out: running the eval and encrypting it (until #828 only a read rule keeps builders away from the folder; not built yet, #798)

Represents: fn-798
